messages.author: 7c8a33455cb7050c
messages.subject: Status of the mean.UD function
parts:
Hi Chris, 

The 20210728  Package 'ctmm' documentation for the mean.UD functions indicates that the confidence intervals are not yet calculated correctly.  I'm using the github development version of ctmm, and have calculated a mean from a list of akde's, and they appear to have 95% confidence intervals.  Does this mean they are now being calculated correctly in the dev version (0.6.2) and the documentation just hadn't caught up with all the work you have done in the last year?

My objective is to calculate an average akde for a herd of caribou while they are range resident on their wintering grounds using ctmm models.  Is my approach appropriate in that I would calculate individual akde, then use the mean function to get a herd boundary?  

Thanks, Robin

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Status of the mean.UD function
parts:
Hi Robin,

The uncertainty is now propagated correctly. I will update the documentation. Thanks.

Your approach is appropriate. This summer/fall, I will be adding the capability to calculate population ranges directly from the tracking data, with weights and bandwidth optimized for population range estimation, which will improve the population estimates. The only other ingredient then missing is correlated movement models for individuals in the same herd, which is probably a few years out.

Best,
Chris
